R03.label: RECONSTRUCTED FOR EVALUATION FROM PUBLISHED RECORDS — NOT AN ORIGINAL SYSTEM EXPORT
R03.construction: Reconstructed record. Compiled from the ESO technical report (Table 1 NGET/MeteoGroup rows and section 4.1), the NGET report in Appendix C (sections 1.1, 1.2, 2.2, 3.1-3.5, 4.1), the ESO answers to E3C questions in Appendix M (Q30) and Ofgem 3.18. Sections A-F restate published record values; ESO Table 1 times are written as ISO-8601 BST (+01:00) because the ESO executive summary dates the event at 4:52pm, while times whose clock basis no source states (section B2, section E) are kept as printed without an offset. The R03 clock line says that the B3/section C BST reading is an inference from that 4:52pm anchor and that only times without such an anchor are marked 'clock basis not stated' (the ESO 4.1 time 16:50:44 for Blyth-Eccles-Stella West has no anchor and conflicts with the Appendix M time 16:43:25, so both stay unlabelled in section E). Section D keeps measured magnitudes only; interpretations and compliance judgements (NGET, ESO, Ofgem) are in section G, in the assessing party's own wording. Section E lists both published times for the Blyth-Eccles-Stella West trip, which conflict, without resolving them; since bundle 1.1.0 there is no compiler's note pointing out the conflict (readers compare the two times themselves). Generator trips, frequency landmarks and demand disconnection are deliberately excluded.

S01.label: SYNTHESISED FOR EVALUATION — NOT REAL EVIDENCE
S01.construction: Synthesised record. Event-log entries restate values and times published in the Ørsted report (APP Appendix D, Figure 3-5 descriptions) and the Ørsted rows of ESO Table 1; BST times are written in UTC (Z). The operator report labels no clock: it writes the same instants as 16:52:33:xxx and, once, as 15.52.33.xxx; the one-hour difference is read as BST and UTC, and the S01 clock line states that this is an inference. The earlier oscillation time is an estimate (event time minus the reported 10 minutes). Log entries carry no times more precise than the operator publishes: the TIP voltage dip (dated only 'at 16:52') takes the .490 end of the steady-voltage interval and is tagged [estimated], and the 20 kV collection-system voltage, which has no time of its own, is bracketed .700Z-.835Z and tagged [estimated] (notes (b) and (c)). Since bundle 1.1.0 the record gives one clock-basis line (BST = UTC+01:00) and no per-entry UTC/BST equivalences, and it no longer states the 799 - 62 MW reduction; readers convert times and compute the loss themselves. Causal statements and mechanisms (for example WTG overcurrent protection as the de-load mechanism, first established in the operator's 5 September report) appear only in the dated, attributed post-event annotations (Ørsted report 2019-09-05, ESO report 2019-09-06, Ofgem report 2020-01-03). Nothing about other generators or frequency landmarks is included.

Single clock-basis line: UTC with Z, BST = UTC+01:00; the operator labels no clock, so the UTC reading is stated as an inference
segments.transformation: The operator report writes the same instants as 16:52:33:xxx and once as 15.52.33.xxx, labelling neither; the BST/UTC reading rests on the one-hour difference and on the ESO timeline (16:52:33.728, dated 4:52pm local time). Only the resulting basis and the inference are stated in the record.

S04.label: SYNTHESISED FOR EVALUATION — NOT REAL EVIDENCE
S04.construction: Synthesised account in two parts. Part 1 is a role-level, chronological shift narrative restating only published facts (ESO 4.2 Little Barford, the RWE SOE in APP Appendix E, Ofgem 3.25-3.29); no names, conversations, readings or clock times are added and no illustrative values are used. Part 2 gives attributed post-event statements, each in its source's order: the RWE preliminary findings dated 30 August 2019 (UPS, steam turbine, gas turbines) and Ofgem 3.28-3.29 dated 3 January 2020, as verbatim quotes or close paraphrase. Since bundle 1.1.0 the account carries no builder classification (no known/not known, established/not established or hypothesis labels); the sources' own words ('RWE's hypothesis is', 'is ongoing', 'For reasons presently unknown', 'We have established', 'has not been established', 'preliminary view') carry the epistemic status. Deliberately not carried into the pack (flagged for the domain reviewer, criteria D4.3/D4.4): the ESO executive summary (PDF page 4) says the GT1A trip was 'due to high pressure in the steam bypass system following the failure of a bypass valve to operate correctly'. ESO section 4.2 (PDF page 20) and RWE (APP page 46) give the excursion's cause as 'presently unknown', and Ofgem 3.29 states that the root cause of the high pressure conditions has not been established, so the pack keeps it unknown. A submission that asserts a bypass-valve failure as established is not supported by the visible evidence.

sources.quote: The investigation to date has found that all UPS’ at Site have functioned correctly to enable continuity of supply to plant equipment.

sources.quote: Therefore, we do not now believe the UPS’ were related to the subsequent trip.

sources.quote: RWE’s hypothesis is that the UPS’ have initiated a changeover to battery back-up supplies as a consequence of the system disturbance.

sources.quote: The exact characteristic of the power supply to the UPS causing it to switch to battery operation is still to be determined and subject to further investigation.

segments.content: Steam turbine: trip due to speed-signal discrepancy after fault clearance (verbatim); comprehensive investigation ongoing
segments.transformation: First sentence verbatim; second closely paraphrased ('the ST' written as 'the steam turbine').

sources.section: Appendix E – RWE Preliminary Findings (dated 30 August 2019), Steam Turbine
sources.quote: Our investigations have confirmed that the Steam Turbine tripped due to a discrepancy in the speed signals after the point of the Transmission System fault clearance.

sources.section: Appendix E – RWE Preliminary Findings (dated 30 August 2019), Steam Turbine
sources.quote: A comprehensive investigation of hardware, software, fault handling and diagnostic coverage for the conditions, that the ST was subjected to during this rare system disturbance, is ongoing.

segments.content: Gas turbines: GT1A excursion 'for reasons presently unknown', automated trip; systems functioned as expected; GT1B manual trip (verbatim)

sources.section: Appendix E – RWE Preliminary Findings (dated 30 August 2019), Gas Turbines
sources.quote: For reasons presently unknown a high-pressure excursion occurred on GT1A resulting in an automated trip. Given the prevailing conditions all systems functioned as expected. GT1B was manually tripped shortly after as a result of excessive steam pressure.

segments.review_note: Conflicting statement not used: ESO executive summary (PDF page 4, printed page 5) attributes the GT1A trip to 'high pressure in the steam bypass system following the failure of a bypass valve to operate correctly'. Ofgem 3.29 (PDF page 31): 'The root cause of these high pressure conditions has not been established.' Reviewer to decide how D4.3/D4.4 treat a submission citing a bypass-valve failure.

segments.content: Gas turbines: planned bypass-system inspection to help determine the root cause (verbatim)

sources.section: Appendix E – RWE Preliminary Findings (dated 30 August 2019), Gas Turbines
sources.quote: A physical inspection of the bypass system is now planned during the forthcoming outage in September 2019 to help determine the root cause of the pressure excursions.

sources.section: Section 3, Little Barford (3.25-3.29) (3.28)
sources.quote: We have established that the steam turbine tripped initially because of a discrepancy in the three independent speed sensors on the turbine. This discrepancy exceeded the tolerance of the control system, causing the generator to automatically shut down. The root cause of the discrepancy in the speed sensors has not been established.

sources.section: Section 3, Little Barford (3.25-3.29) (3.29)
sources.quote: Given the sequence of events and in absence of an established root cause, it is our preliminary view that the steam turbine’s anomalous speed readings and the resulting trip were due to the transmission network fault following the lightning strike.
